title: The Seven Principles and Tailoring

header.html: Explain the seven principles; explain how and why the principles provide the basis for applying PRINCE2, which factors influence how the method is tailored, who is responsible and how tailoring decisions are documented
the official PRINCE2 7 Foundation syllabus (PeopleCert), learning outcome 2

toc.title: What each principle means in practice

html:
1The seven principles

The principles are the guiding obligations and good practices that determine whether a project is really being managed with PRINCE2. If a principle is not applied, the project is not using PRINCE2.

# Principle In one line
1 Ensure continued business justification There is a documented reason for the project that stays valid all the way
2 Learn from experience Seek, record and apply lessons throughout
3 Define roles, responsibilities and relationships Everyone knows who does what and who they work with
4 Manage by stages Plan, monitor and control the project stage by stage
5 Manage by exception Set tolerances; escalate only when they would be exceeded
6 Focus on products Concentrate on what is delivered and its quality, not just on activity
7 Tailor to suit the project Adapt PRINCE2 to the project's context
Exam tip

. Learn the seven names in this order. Scenario questions describe a behavior and ask which principle it shows or breaks.

2What each principle means in practice

Principle In practice
Continued business justification A business case exists, is approved, and is checked at every decision point; the project stops if it is no longer justified
Learn from experience Review past lessons at the start, record new ones in the lessons log, and share them at the end
Roles, responsibilities, relationships A project management team structure covers the business, user and supplier interests
Manage by stages The project has at least two management stages (initiation and one more); the board authorizes each stage
Manage by exception Authority is delegated within tolerances; an exception goes up to the next level
Focus on products Product descriptions with quality criteria are agreed before work starts
Tailor Adapt the method, documenting the decision, but keep the principles

3Tailoring

Tailoring means adapting PRINCE2 so it fits the project's size, complexity, importance, team capability, risk and environment, without losing its principles.

Can be tailored Cannot be dropped
Processes can be simplified or carried out in more detail The principles
Terminology can be changed to match organizational standards The intent of each practice (each must be addressed)
Practices are adapted to the project The need for the project board to remain accountable
Roles can be combined in sensible ways A business case and control by the board

Some roles can be combined, but not all combinations are allowed: for example, the person who manages the project should not also provide project assurance of their own work. [Verify live]

Who is responsible, and where is it recorded: the project manager is responsible for tailoring the method to the project, and tailoring decisions are documented in the project initiation documentation (PID), which the project board approves. [Verify live]

Exam tip

. Tailoring never means leaving out a principle. An option that says a practice can be ignored completely or that any combination of roles is allowed is wrong.

Exam tip

. Scenario questions describe a behavior (no stage approval, no business case review, no product definition). Name the principle that behavior breaks.

4Exam Q&A

4.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A project board approves the business case, then never looks at it again until the end. Which principle is being broken?

  • AManage by stages
  • BFocus on products
  • CTailor to suit the project
  • DEnsure continued business justification
Show the answer

Answer: D. The justification must be checked and remain valid throughout.

S2A project manager asks the board to approve a plan for the next stage before the stage begins. Which principle does this support?

  • ALearn from experience
  • BManage by exception
  • CManage by stages
  • DDefine roles, responsibilities and relationships
Show the answer

Answer: C. The board authorizes work stage by stage.

S3Which statements about tailoring are CORRECT? (1) Processes can be simplified or carried out in more detail. (2) Terminology can be changed to match organizational standards. (3) A principle can be left out if the project is small. (4) Project team members can combine any roles at all.

  • A1 and 2
  • B2 and 3
  • C3 and 4
  • D1 and 4
Show the answer

Answer: A. Processes and terminology can be tailored; principles are not dropped and not every role combination is allowed.

S4Identify the missing word. The principle "manage by [ ? ]" delegates authority within agreed tolerances.

  • AStages
  • BProducts
  • CException
  • DExperience
Show the answer

Answer: C. Manage by exception uses tolerances and escalation.

S5A team writes a product description with quality criteria before building the product. Which principle does this show?

  • ATailor to suit the project
  • BManage by stages
  • CLearn from experience
  • DFocus on products
Show the answer

Answer: D. Defining the product and its quality first is a product focus.

S6Where are tailoring decisions documented?

  • AIn the daily log only
  • BIn the end project report only
  • CIn the PID
  • DIn the risk register
Show the answer

Answer: C. Tailoring decisions are documented in the PID.

4.2 Recall questions

R1Name the seven principles.

Show the answer

Ensure continued business justification; learn from experience; define roles, responsibilities and relationships; manage by stages; manage by exception; focus on products; tailor to suit the project.

R2What is the minimum number of management stages?

Show the answer

Two (the initiation stage and at least one more).

R3What does manage by exception use?

Show the answer

Tolerances, with escalation when they would be exceeded.

R4What is tailoring?

Show the answer

Adapting PRINCE2 to fit the project's context without losing the principles.

R5Who is responsible for tailoring?

Show the answer

The project manager (the project board approves the PID that records it).

R6If a principle is not applied, what does that mean?

Show the answer

The project is not being managed using PRINCE2.

5Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Principles business justification, learn from experience, roles, stages, exception, products, tailor
Stages at least two
Exception tolerances and escalation
Tailoring adapt, document in the PID, never drop principles
